era: Super Famicom through modern action JRPG
summary: tri-Ace and Square Enix's science-fantasy action RPG series, including the mainline console games, remakes/remasters, Blue Sphere, and the mobile/social spin-offs.

entries.title: Star Ocean

emulation.emulator: Snes9x or bsnes for original comparison; PPSSPP for PSP comparison
emulation.notes: Use the native PS4 release for the main run.

primary.why: First Departure R is the modern HD remaster of the PSP remake, which itself added new art, animated cutscenes, fully voiced dialogue, new playable characters, and international localization to the original Japan-only Super Famicom game.
primary.how_to_play: Play Star Ocean: First Departure R on PlayStation 4, or on PlayStation 5 through backward compatibility. Use the Switch version only if portability matters.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Japan-only Super Famicom release.
all_releases.reason: skip: historical original, but the remake/remaster adds official English support, new content, and modern presentation.

all_releases.fidelity: PSP remake with new artwork, animated cutscenes, full voice work, and new playable characters.
all_releases.reason: skip: important remake, but superseded by First Departure R on modern platforms.

all_releases.fidelity: HD remaster of First Departure with selectable portraits, voice options, rebalanced difficulty, and faster world-map movement.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity modern route for the expanded remake.

all_releases.fidelity: Switch release of First Departure R.
all_releases.reason: skip: same modern remaster content, but PS4/PS5 is the better fixed-screen capture route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The modern First Departure R route is both the most complete official route and the best-fidelity route.

entries.remaster_caveats: First Departure R is a remaster of the PSP remake, not a pure port of the Super Famicom original.

entries.title: Star Ocean: The Second Story
entries.definitive_edition: Star Ocean: The Second Story R

emulation.emulator: DuckStation for original PlayStation comparison; PPSSPP for Second Evolution comparison
emulation.notes: Use the native PC remake for the main run.

primary.version: Star Ocean: The Second Story R
primary.why: The Second Story R is the modern remake with 2.5D visuals, new battle mechanics, full Japanese and English voice overs, original and rearranged music, fast travel, and PC capture flexibility.
primary.how_to_play: Play Star Ocean: The Second Story R on Steam/Windows. Use the PS5 version if a console route is preferred.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PlayStation release.
all_releases.reason: skip: original route, but superseded for the main run by Second Story R.

all_releases.fidelity: PSP remake/revision of The Second Story.
all_releases.reason: skip: portable remake route, but superseded by the 2023 remake.

all_releases.fidelity: Japanese digital ports of Second Evolution.
all_releases.reason: skip: older remake route, superseded by Second Story R.

all_releases.fidelity: Modern 2.5D remake with PC settings and Steam release.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity and most complete modern route.

all_releases.fidelity: Console releases of The Second Story R.
all_releases.reason: skip: same remake content, but PC is the best capture/settings route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The Second Story R is the modern high-fidelity and complete route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Second Story R is a remake rather than the original PlayStation presentation.

entries.title: Star Ocean: Blue Sphere
entries.definitive_edition: Original Game Boy Color release for preservation play

emulation.notes: Use integer scaling and original GBC aspect ratio.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Clean upscaled Game Boy Color output.

primary.version: Original Japanese GBC release via mGBA
primary.why: Blue Sphere is a Japan-only direct sequel to The Second Story. A 2009 mobile remake exists, but the Game Boy Color version is the stable preservation route with documented single-player and multiplayer support.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally dumped Game Boy Color cartridge image in mGBA with integer scaling. Expect Japanese text unless using a separately sourced translation patch.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Japan-only handheld release.
all_releases.reason: primary: stable preservation route for the complete original game.

all_releases.fidelity: Japan-only mobile remake with new graphics, controls, and retooled battle system.
all_releases.reason: skip: higher-presentation mobile remake, but not the most practical preserved route for a full playthrough.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The mobile remake has updated presentation, but the Game Boy Color original is the more stable preservation route.

entries.remaster_caveats: The mobile remake is Japan-only and not treated as the practical primary route.

entries.title: Star Ocean: Till the End of Time

primary.why: The Director's Cut fixed issues and added bonus features such as new characters, dungeons, battle trophies, and versus mode; PCSX2 gives the highest-fidelity route for that complete version.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally dumped Director's Cut PS2 disc image in PCSX2 with high internal resolution and deinterlacing. The PS4 digital route is convenient, but PCSX2 gives more capture control.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Japanese PS2 release.
all_releases.reason: skip: superseded by the Director's Cut version with fixes and bonus features.

all_releases.fidelity: Two-disc Director's Cut with bonus features and PCSX2 upscaling available.
all_releases.reason: primary: most complete documented version and best emulated-fidelity route.

all_releases.fidelity: Official PS4 digital release of the PS2 title.
all_releases.reason: skip: official convenience route, but PCSX2 has more capture and scaling control.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The Director's Cut route is both most complete and highest-fidelity through PCSX2.

entries.remaster_caveats: No full remake is documented; PS4 is an official legacy digital route.

entries.title: Star Ocean: The Last Hope
entries.definitive_edition: Star Ocean: The Last Hope - 4K & Full HD Remaster

emulation.emulator: RPCS3 or Xenia only for historical comparison
emulation.notes: Use the native Steam remaster for the main run.

primary.why: The Windows 4K & Full HD Remaster is based on the later International content path and supports modern PC output; the PS3 International version added dual voices, original illustrated portraits, and extra music beyond the Xbox 360 release.
primary.how_to_play: Play Star Ocean: The Last Hope - 4K & Full HD Remaster on Steam/Windows at the highest stable resolution and frame-rate settings.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Xbox 360 release.
all_releases.reason: skip: original release, but lacks International additions and modern 4K/PC remaster support.

all_releases.fidelity: International version with dual voices, original illustrated portraits, and additional music.
all_releases.reason: skip: content-important version, but superseded for fidelity by the 4K & Full HD Remaster.

all_releases.fidelity: 4K & Full HD Remaster with PC output and settings.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity route and best capture platform.

all_releases.fidelity: 4K & Full HD Remaster on PS4/PS4 Pro.
all_releases.reason: skip: same remaster family, but PC has the best settings and capture flexibility.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The 4K & Full HD Remaster is the best modern route for both fidelity and International-version content.

entries.remaster_caveats: The remaster modernizes The Last Hope International rather than the original Xbox 360-only release.

entries.title: Star Ocean: Material Trader

primary.why: Material Trader was a free-to-play card and item-creation RPG for GREE; the service was terminated in February 2014 and the application was delisted, so no current normal play route exists.
primary.how_to_play: No current official play route is documented. Preserve through archival footage, screenshots, and contemporary documentation unless a lawful offline build is recovered.

all_releases.fidelity: Free-to-play mobile/social service, now terminated and delisted.
all_releases.reason: primary: only documented release route, preserved historically rather than as a currently playable game.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The only official route was a terminated service; completeness is archival rather than playable.

entries.remaster_caveats: No offline edition, port, or remaster is documented.

entries.title: Star Ocean: Integrity and Faithlessness

emulation.notes: Use native PS4/PS5 playback for the main run.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PS4 output, with PS5 backward compatibility as a stability route.

primary.why: The PS4 version has higher resolution and frame rate than the Japan-only PS3 version and is the only version released outside Japan.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation 4 release, preferably on PlayStation 5 through backward compatibility for the most stable console capture.

all_releases.fidelity: PS4 release with higher resolution and framerate than PS3.
all_releases.reason: primary: best-fidelity and international route.

all_releases.fidelity: Japan-only PS3 version.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower technical ceiling and not released outside Japan.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No content-exclusive PS3 route is documented; PS4 is the best route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No PC port or remaster is documented.

entries.title: Star Ocean: Anamnesis
entries.definitive_edition: Offline version where available, historical live service otherwise

emulation.emulator: Android device or emulator if a lawful offline install is available
emulation.notes: Do not expect full live-service content.

primary.why: Anamnesis was a mobile free-to-play action RPG released for Android and iOS; the global and Japanese services shut down, but an offline version remains documented with the first three episodes and acquired character models.
primary.how_to_play: If already available on a device/account, use the offline version for limited archival access. The full live-service game is no longer normally playable.

all_releases.fidelity: Mobile free-to-play release, later shut down with a limited offline version.
all_releases.reason: primary: only documented platform route; offline mode is archival and incomplete compared with the live service.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The full live service was shut down; the documented offline version is only a limited archival route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No complete offline remaster or current live-service route is documented.

entries.title: Star Ocean: The Divine Force

primary.why: The Divine Force shipped on PC and modern consoles; Windows offers the highest settings and capture flexibility for the full game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Steam/Windows release at the highest stable settings. PS5 or Xbox Series X/S are the best console alternatives.

all_releases.fidelity: PC release with graphics/settings flexibility.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity and most flexible capture route.

all_releases.fidelity: Current-generation console releases.
all_releases.reason: skip: strong console alternatives, but PC has the highest settings flexibility.

all_releases.fidelity: Last-generation console releases.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower hardware ceiling than PC/current-generation consoles and no unique content documented.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No platform-exclusive content split is documented.

entries.remaster_caveats: No later definitive edition is documented.
